description:
src/memory.rs:484-532 (query_objects impl) uses 'as' casts across signed/unsigned/width boundaries:

    let total = ids.len() as u64;                              // line 504 — usize -> u64
    let start = if position >= 0 {
        (position as usize).min(ids.len())                     // line 513 — i64 -> usize
    } else {
        let neg = position.saturating_neg() as usize;          // line 515 — i64 -> usize
        ids.len().saturating_sub(neg)
    };
    ids = ids[start..]
        .iter()
        .take(limit.map_or(usize::MAX, |n| n as usize))        // line 521 — u64 -> usize
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    Ok(QueryResult::new(ids, start as u64, ...))                // line 527 — usize -> u64

Plus memory.rs:443 and :862:
    if relevant.len() as u64 > max { ... }                     // usize -> u64

Idiomatic Rust on 64-bit and 32-bit targets behaves differently for u64 -> usize: on a 32-bit target, 'limit as usize' silently truncates. usize -> u64 widening is fine on any current target. i64 -> usize truncates and reinterprets negatives. 'as' silently lossy-converts in all these cases.

The cookie-cutter sibling jmap-mail-server uses the same 'as' pattern (memory.rs same construct, ~line equivalents), so this is a canonical-template issue — fix at the canonical and propagate.

What goes wrong:
- u64-to-usize on 32-bit targets: a request with limit > 4GB elements silently truncates the limit. For an in-memory demo backend this is theoretical; for a production backend implemented from the same template, it's a request-truncation bug.
- i64-to-usize negative cast: position.saturating_neg() pivots i64::MIN to i64::MAX, then 'as usize' on that is target-dependent (truncates on 32-bit). Already partially flagged by JMAP-ayoz.14 as 'unusual'; this finding extends it to the broader cast pattern.

Idiomatic alternatives:
- u64 -> usize: usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) — caps cleanly at the architecture limit.
- usize -> u64: u64::from(n.try_into().unwrap_or(u64::MAX)) or simply 'n as u64' is widening-safe on supported targets, but a clippy::cast_lossless lint can be enabled to force From::from.
- i64 -> usize: explicit guard 'if position < 0 { 0 } else { usize::try_from(position).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) }'.

This is a clippy-priority finding (P3, type=chore) because the targets shipped today are 64-bit; the canonical-template question is the real issue. The metadata-server sibling inherits the cast pattern from jmap-mail-server.
title: memory.rs query_objects uses unchecked 'as' casts between usize/u64/i64; prefer try_from
